tie_break: 1. larger f_dd_off; 2. larger f_gates; 3. smaller max_q S_T2; 4. lexicographically smallest tuple of physical qubits
method: A candidate patch is an embedding of the routed circuit's CZ interaction graph into the device coupling graph; relabelling the frozen circuit along it changes no gate, no angle, no CZ count and no classical-bit mapping, only which physical qubit plays which role.  The enumeration is exhaustive and deterministic (pattern nodes by descending degree then index, host nodes ascending).  Every scored quantity comes from scripts/h0_idle_model.py (schedule, budgets, f_on_record, predictions) applied to the relabelled circuit on the record; the identity embedding is asserted equal to that script's own output to 1e-12.  The yield is y = 0.82 f + (1 - f) a (manual Step 4.4, skqd.skqd.yield_model).
finding: On committed record ibm_kingston_20260930T2255Z.json (1454 candidate patches over 156 qubits) the best patch is [82, 83, 96, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 117, 125, 126] with f (DD off) 5.622e-02; incumbent not scorable on this record: qubit 146 has no T1_s, so no gain over the transpiler's patch is defined.  The H0 calibration records cover only the qubits and edges the frozen set already uses, so the committed-record search is a lower bound on what a full-device read would find; the selection rule therefore has to be run on a full-device target read (free, no QPU time) on the day.
